initial_prompt: Can you write me a poem about the feeling of watching someone you love slowly lose their memory to dementia?

messages.content: Can you write me a poem about the feeling of watching someone you love slowly lose their memory to dementia?

# The Forgetting

I am learning to answer
the same question
like it's the first time,
because for you, it is.

Your hands still know
how to fold a napkin,
how to hold a cup—
the body remembers
what the mind releases.

You called me by your sister's name today.
I didn't correct you.
She died in 1963,
and for a moment
you had her back.

I watch you leave
in increments,
like a house
whose lights go dark
room by room—
someone still home
but fewer windows
to wave from.

The cruelest part
is not the forgetting.
It's the moments you remember
that you forget,
and I see the terror
of a woman waking
in a stranger's life.

I hold your hand.
You hold mine back.
This, at least,
needs no memory—
just pressure answering pressure,
warmth recognizing warmth.

I am learning
that love is not
being known.
It is showing up
to the same door
every day,
even when no one
remembers
knocking.
